To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the band-to-band impact ionization in Si-MOS is very sensitive to the electric field distribution, and the electric field distribution in turn is very sensitive to device geometry and doping profile.
the tunneling current is strongly dependent on both the electric field and the potential in the critical area and that the electric field varies significantly along the tunneling trajectory.

(a) the band-to-band generation in Si-MOS transistors is strongly affected by the nonuniform electric field in the channel region; and (b) the band-toband tunneling generation rate is strongly affected by nonuniform electric field along the channel direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a two-dimensional numerical model of the interband tunneling effect in Si-MOS devices.
the modeling of the interband tunneling in MOSFETs.
the modeling and simulation of the band-to- band tunneling current in the MOSFET.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the band-to-band impact ionization is a very complex process, which is strongly influenced by the electric field distribution and the potential profile in the tunneling region.
the band-to-band impact ionization model is not a reliable method for the calculation of the bandgap narrowing in heavily doped silicon.
the band-to-band generation in Si MOSFET's is not a simple function of the applied gate voltage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two-band k.p model is a very powerful tool in the analysis of the tunneling phenomena.
we have developed a numerical model to simulate band-to-band tunnel current and have applied it in the analysis of the band-to band tunnel current in Si MOSFET.
the tunneling is strongly affected by the nonuniform electric field distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tunneling effect in the MOSFET is not only dependent on the electric field but also on the potential distribution in the critical region.
the effect of the nonuniform field distribution in the tunneling region on the tunneling probability must be taken into account in the numerical simulation of the band-toband tunneling.
the band-to-band-tunneling effect is not only strongly dependent on the terminal voltages, but also on the electric field and potential distribution in the critical areas.
